issue.title: Time sync issue between SONiC and FRR stack

failure.body:
#### Description
There is a time sync issue between SONIC and the FRR stack. For instance, Inside vtysh, "Show interface status" CLI output and FRR log always shows the UTC timestamp which does not match with the SONIC in case a specific time zone is configured on the SONIC side.

#### Steps to reproduce the issue:
1. Configure specific timezone except UTC in SONIC via "timedatectl set-timezone <>" CLI
2. Flap the UP interface
3. Go inside vtysh and check the output of "show interface <>" for the flap timestamp
4. Alternatively check the zebra.log file

#### Describe the results you received:
LOGS:
root@SN2100-Leaf1:~# show clock
Wed 14 Dec 2022 <IPV6> AM UTC
root@SN2100-Leaf1:~# timedatectl set-timezone America/Los_Angeles  ========> configured as PST ( using set timezone)
root@SN2100-Leaf1:~#
root@SN2100-Leaf1:~#
root@SN2100-Leaf1:~#
root@SN2100-Leaf1:~# show clock

root@SN2100-Leaf1:~# config interface startup Ethernet0
root@SN2100-Leaf1:~# vtysh

% Unknown command: date

Interface Ethernet0 is up, line protocol is down

Dec 14 <IPV6>.953850 SN2100-Leaf1 ERR bgp#zebra[35]: [EC 4043309093] netlink-dp (NS 0) error: Network is down, type=RTM_NEWNEXTHOP(104), seq=165, pid=2957759799

Dec 14 <IPV6>.306529 SN2100-Leaf1 ERR bgp#zebra[35]: [EC 4043309074] Failed to install Nexthop ID (6) into the kernel

#### Describe the results you expected:
Expecting a time sync between SONIC timezone and the FRR stack so that there will not be any confusion while interpreting the logs.

resolution.title: Timezone sync issue between the host and containers
resolution.description:
#### Why I did it
To fix the timezone sync issue between the containers and the host. If a certain timezone has been configured on the host (SONIC) then the expectation is to reflect the same across all the containers.

This will fix [Issue:13046](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/13046).

For instance, a PST timezone has been set on the host and if the user checks the link flap logs (inside the FRR), it shows the UTC timestamp. Ideally, it should be PST.

LOGS:
root@sonic:~# show clock
Mon Feb 7 <IPV6> PST 2022 ======== configured as PST ( using set timezone)

sonic# vtysh
sonic# show interface Ethernet0
Interface Ethernet0 is up, line protocol is up
Link ups: 4 last: 2022/02/03 <IPV6>.34 ----> shows UTC timestamp
Link downs: 6 last: 2022/02/03 <IPV6>.35 ---->
vrf: default
index 26 metric 0 mtu 9126 speed 0
flags: <UP,BROADCAST,RUNNING,MULTICAST>
Type: Unknown
HWaddr: <IPV6>
inet [<IP>/31](https://nam10.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=http%3A%2F%2F172.21.227.64%2F31&data=05%7C01%7Cnmoray%40ebay.com%7C9b88b81e54ac402f3f4a08da3e1ed96e%7C46326bff992841a0baca17c16c94ea99%7C0%7C0%7C637890599471979401%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C3000%7C%7C%7C&sdata=lyPmxXhB8QOLP2JXtoCMMxDZ%2FuTFGzKCtIoJeukE%2BcA%3D&reserved=0)
inet6 fd0a:200💯:340/127
inet6 fe80::<IPV6>/64
Interface Type Other

#### How I did it
Mounted host's /etc/timezone file on all the containers to  find out the presently configured timezone during the docker initialisation phase. Later, based on the host's timezone, create a symbolic link at runtime inside each of the containers (/etc/localtime). This way, we can avoid mounting the symlink on the containers.

#### How to verify it
root@sonic:~# timedatectl set-timezone America/Los_Angeles
root@sonic:~#
root@sonic:~#
root@sonic:~# date
Fri 28 Apr 2023 <IPV6> AM PDT

root@sonic:~# cat /etc/timezone
America/Los_Angeles
root@sonic:~# ls /etc/localtime -l
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root 41 Apr 28 10:22 /etc/localtime -> ../usr/share/zoneinfo/America/Los_Angeles
root@sonic:~# docker exec -it bgp bash
root@sonic:/# date
Fri Apr 28 <IPV6> UTC 2023
root@sonic:/# exit
exit

root@sonic:~# config reload -f
